evidence.positive: Against the running app at localhost:55752 (image built from 2cd9104ea), created a mayo-mayo patient and case carrying exactly p-whipple + p-biliary-stent-placement via POST /api/admin/patients/ and .../operations/create (pmrn or2776-fake-7b1c5782-d29b-4497-b047-14054146ae43, caseId 98502). GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/98502/antibiotic-candidates returned outcome=RECOMMENDED with recommended=step1:PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM, while the same response shows the underlying configuration as p-biliary-stent-placement[CEFAZOLIN -> CIPROFLOXACIN] and p-whipple[none] - i.e. the pip-tazo answer can only have come from the combination table. App log: 'g.o.s.ProcedureCombinationPathwayService : Operation 01a03f6c-23f6-74d8-b655-7b9b6aa1c58c matches the antibiotic pathway for procedure combination [p-biliary-stent-placement, p-whipple]'. Rank 1 of the ticket's table was confirmed by adding a Penicillin/ANAPHYLAXIS allergy to the same patient: recommended became step2:LEVOFLOXACIN+METRONIDAZOLE+VANCOMYCIN with contraindicated=["PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM"].
evidence.negative: Built three further mayo-mayo cases and read the same debugger endpoint. p-whipple alone (case 95782): outcome=NOT_CONFIGURED, recommended=(none), log 'Operation ... has no antibiotic pathways to walk under tenant TenantKey[value=mayo-mayo]: [p-whipple drug=0 none=false] (tenant holds 463 pathways)' - the combination did not leak onto a single-procedure case. p-biliary-stent-placement alone (case 88369): outcome=RECOMMENDED, recommended=step1:CEFAZOLIN - the stent keeps its own configuration and does not pick up pip-tazo. p-whipple + p-biliary-stent-placement + p-appendectomy (case 48588): outcome=SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT, recommended=(none), and NO 'matches the antibiotic pathway for procedure combination' line was emitted for that operation, confirming the exact-set match rather than a subset match. Control: p-pancreatectomy + p-biliary-stent-placement (case 38608) still returns step1:PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM, so the pre-existing combination was not disturbed. At the user-facing layer: selecting m-piperacillin-tazobactam-3.375 on case 98502 returned results=[] (no wrong-antibiotic alert), and selecting m-cefazolin on the biliary-alone and whipple-alone cases produced no a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic alert either.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway instance built from main at 2cd9104ea, tenant mayo-mayo.

Positive: a case carrying exactly p-whipple and p-biliary-stent-placement resolves to PIPERACILLIN-TAZOBACTAM at rank 0, and to LEVOFLOXACIN + METRONIDAZOLE + VANCOMYCIN at rank 1 once a penicillin anaphylaxis allergy rules the first step out. Selecting cefazolin on that case now fires the wrong-antibiotic alert with "Piperacillin-Tazobactam is recommended - For Biliary Stent Placement and Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple)".

Negative: p-whipple alone still reports not configured, the biliary stent alone still recommends cefazolin, and adding a third procedure (appendectomy) drops back to the per-procedure walk and suppresses the recommendation, so the combination is matched as an exact set. The existing p-pancreatectomy pairing is unchanged.

Red check, done twice and reverted both times. The pre-fix version of ProcedureCombinationPathwayService was compiled and swapped into the running container: the same case then recommended plain cefazolin with no alert, which is the reported bug, while the pancreatectomy pairing still worked. The shipped class was restored, checksums re-confirmed, and the positive case re-run green. Separately the PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM medication category was renamed, which made the case fall back to cefazolin and logged the combination as unrecommendable by name; the rename was reverted and the recommendation returned.

Not exercised: the same procedure pair under a non-Mayo tenant, since no other seeded tenant carries these two procedure types.

Automation: existing unit and configuration-backed tests already cover both shipped combinations for the main recommendation. Follow-up will parameterize the allergy-fallback and third-procedure tests over the whipple pair as well, and add a selection-rule test driven by the shipped combination rather than mocked candidates.
